data.content_ref: inline:The target answers the cross-city part by naming TWO independent mechanisms—thermal mass/storage-release AND street-canyon sky-view trapping—then asserts the gap is larger in dense cities specifically because of the geometry. But that only relocates the question: the problem asks what SINGLE mechanism best explains why the night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others, and the target does not identify one dominant cross-city modulator. Instead it bundles two causal factors (stored sensible heat release + reduced sky view longwave trapping) and treats the second as the cross-city driver while still relying on the first for the base warming, so the 'single mechanism' requirement is not genuinely met.
